**4B.5 Research Note**

Overall judgment: **No**. The 2024 record shows limited procedural restraint and one reactive inquiry, but the dominant pattern is intimidation, media pressure, judicial politicization, and coercive management of opponents and civic space. I found no reliable 2024 evidence of a genuine effort to avoid personality-driven politics or party/state capture.

- [Shehbaz Sharif to be coalition candidate for next Pakistan PM -spokeswoman](https://theprint.in/world/shehbaz-sharif-to-be-coalition-candidate-for-next-pakistan-pm-spokeswoman/1965379/) - **Reuters**, 2024-02-14. Claim: After a hung parliament, Sharif’s return depended on coalition bargaining, which is the main weak-positive sign that power was still procedurally contestable rather than personally monopolized. **QIDs:** 4B.5, 4B.1, 4B.2.

- [Pakistan to investigate army’s meddling in judiciary, law minister says](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/3/28/pakistan-to-investigate-armys-meddling-in-judiciary-law-minister-says) - **Reuters via Al Jazeera**, 2024-03-28. Claim: After six High Court judges alleged ISI intimidation, the government said it would form an inquiry commission. This is the clearest positive oversight item, but it is reactive and does not show a durable commitment to keeping neutral institutions unpoliticized. **QIDs:** 4B.5, 4B.4, 3B.4.

- [Mohtasib resolves 193,028 complaints, provides relief of Rs 48.98 billion](https://president.gov.pk/mohtasib-resolves-193028-complaints-provides-relief-of-rs-4898-billion-2) - **President of Pakistan**, 2024-02-07. Claim: The federal ombudsman handled a large volume of complaints and provided relief, showing complaint-handling infrastructure was active. This is a weak positive because it reflects inherited institutional capacity more than Sharif’s empowerment of independent oversight. **QIDs:** 4B.5, 4B.4.

- [Pakistan: Election-day internet shutdown is a reckless attack on people’s rights](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/02/pakistan-election-day-internet-shutdown-is-a-reckless-attack-on-peoples-rights/) - **Amnesty International**, 2024-02-08. Claim: The election-day telecom and mobile internet shutdown chilled expression, assembly, and monitoring. That is direct evidence of a coercive political environment incompatible with a clean anti-intimidation or anti-politicization reading. **QIDs:** 4B.5, 4B.3, 4B.2, 3B.8, 3B.9.

- [Pakistan: Widening Crackdown on Dissent](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/01/11/pakistan-widening-crackdown-dissent) - **Human Rights Watch**, 2024-01-11. Claim: HRW said the government clamped down on dissenting media, the opposition, and NGOs, with pressure that deepened self-censorship. This is strong evidence against avoiding intimidation and against keeping neutral institutions neutral. **QIDs:** 4B.5, 4B.3, 4B.4, 4B.2, 3B.8.

- [Social media platform X blocked in Pakistan over national security, ministry says](https://www.investing.com/news/economy/social-media-platform-x-blocked-in-pakistan-over-national-security-ministry-says-3382313) - **Reuters**, 2024-04-17. Claim: The state acknowledged blocking X on national-security grounds, directly restricting criticism, reporting, and monitoring. That is evidence of politicizing a neutral communications environment rather than preserving it. **QIDs:** 4B.5, 4B.3, 4B.2, 3B.8.

- [Pakistan: The new Peaceful Assembly and Public Order Act threatens the right to protest](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/09/pakistan-the-new-peaceful-assembly-and-public-order-act-threatens-the-right-to-protest/) - **Amnesty International**, 2024-09-09. Claim: Amnesty said the government rushed through a law that criminalized peaceful assembly and expanded powers to restrict gatherings. This points to state capture of the protest arena, not avoidance of arbitrary loyalty tests or intimidation. **QIDs:** 4B.5, 4B.3, 4B.4, 4B.2, 3B.8.

- [Pakistan Government Intensifies Crackdown on Political Dissent](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/10/09/pakistan-government-intensifies-crackdown-political-dissent) - **Human Rights Watch**, 2024-10-09. Claim: HRW reported mass arrests, tear gas, roadblocks, and mobile-internet cuts against PTI protesters, including peaceful demonstrators. This is strong evidence of intimidation and coercive use of state power against opponents. **QIDs:** 4B.5, 4B.3, 4B.2, 3B.8, 3B.9, 3B.10.

- [Pakistan’s government curbs judiciary’s power after alleged harassment of MPs](https://www.theguardian.com/world/2024/oct/21/pakistans-government-curbs-judiciarys-power-after-alleged-harassment-of-mps) - **The Guardian**, 2024-10-21. Claim: The 26th Amendment changed senior-judge appointment rules in ways critics said weakened judicial independence, and it passed amid allegations of intimidation and abductions of MPs. This is the clearest negative evidence for politicizing a neutral state institution. **QIDs:** 4B.5, 4B.4, 4B.2.

- [Pakistan report](https://www.ecoi.net/en/document/2128431.html) - **U.S. Department of State**, 2024. Claim: The report says authorities used PEMRA, network access, and government advertising to suppress threatening media and issued notices to journalists and YouTubers for alleged anti-state material. That directly undercuts any claim of avoiding politicization of neutral institutions or arbitrary loyalty policing. **QIDs:** 4B.5, 4B.3, 4B.4, 4B.2.

- [Pakistan: Urgent and transparent investigation needed into deadly crackdown on opposition protesters](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/11/urgent-and-transparent-investigation-needed-into-deadly-crackdown-on-opposition-protesters/) - **Amnesty International**, 2024-11-27. Claim: Amnesty described deaths, mass detentions, shutdowns, and a pattern of intolerance toward peaceful opposition assembly. This is the strongest year-end evidence that the government relied on intimidation rather than neutral, non-personalist governance. **QIDs:** 4B.5, 4B.3, 4B.2, 3B.8, 3B.9, 3B.10.

- [Pakistan’s Imran Khan’s party loses cricket bat electoral symbol](https://theprint.in/world/pakistans-imran-khans-party-loses-cricket-bat-electoral-symbol/1923216/) - **Reuters**, 2024-01-14. Claim: The Supreme Court upheld the Election Commission’s removal of PTI’s bat symbol on technical grounds, which was legally framed but materially disadvantaged Sharif’s main opponent. This is relevant as a sign of party-system engineering rather than clean institutional neutrality. **QIDs:** 4B.5, 4B.2, 4B.1.

**Search gap**

- I found **no reliable 2024 evidence** that Sharif rejected personality-cult politics in any affirmative, documented way.
- I also found **no strong positive evidence** that he avoided arbitrary loyalty tests or depoliticization failures in the media, courts, or protest space.
- The best available positives are procedural and reactive; the stronger record points to intimidation and institutional politicization.
